facts.statement: The genus Venustodus includes six known species: V. argutus, V. leidyi, V. robustus, V. tenuicristatus, V. variabilis, and V. venustus.
facts.quote: * †V. argutus St. John & Worthen, 1875 †V. leidyi St. John & Worthen, 1875 †V. robustus St. John & Worthen, 1875 †V. tenuicristatus St. John & Worthen, 1875 †V. variabilis St. John & Worthen, 1875 †V. venustus Leidy, 1857

facts.statement: The genus Venustodus was first described by St. John and Worthen in 1875.
The type species of the genus Venustodus is Venustodus venustus.
Venustodus is classified either in the family Cochliodontidae or has an indeterminate position within the subclass Holocephali.
facts.quote: It has been assigned either to the family Cochliodontidae or an indeterminate position within the subclass Holocephali

facts.statement: In 1984, researcher Rainer Zangerl suggested that the classification of Venustodus was unknown and that it might not be related to holocephalans.
facts.quote: although in 1984 researcher Rainer Zangerl insisted that nothing is known of the genus' classification and that it may be unrelated to holocephalans

facts.statement: Venustodus lived during the Carboniferous period in Russia and the United States.
facts.quote: Venustodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from the Carboniferous of Russia and the United States

facts.statement: All species of Venustodus were believed to be nektonic marine carnivores.
facts.quote: All species of Venustodus are believed to have been nektonic, marine carnivores

facts.statement: Venustodus lived from the Visean to the Moscovian stages, approximately 346.7 to 307 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Moscovian (346.7 to 307 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Venustodus is the family Cochliodontidae.
